svg.title: Single-cell RNA sequencing: from tissue to an expression matrix
svg.desc: A conceptual overview of 10x Chromium 3′ gene expression. Read steps 1–3 on the top row, then 4–6 on the bottom row. Tissue is dissociated, cells are counted and checked, and microfluidics partitions them into droplets. Molecular tagging, reverse transcription, library preparation, sequencing and software processing lead to a gene-by-cell expression matrix. Cell barcodes identify partitions, UMIs distinguish captured molecules, and sample indices identify libraries. Not to scale.

g.title: A cell suspension, barcoded gel beads, reagents and oil enter a microfluidic chip. The examples below show a droplet with no cells and a doublet with two cells.
The gel bead in a GEM carries capture primers. Different mRNA molecules in one GEM can receive the same partition barcode and different UMIs.

g.text: From tissue to a single-cell expression matrix
